issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Pneumatic.raisePressure(int pressureIncrease) to return boolean, but the solution (and the method implementations) declare raisePressure(...) as void. This mismatch between the specified UML signature and the reference implementation will confuse students: if they follow the UML they will declare a boolean-returning method and need to implement/return a boolean in classes that implement the interface, while the solution/tests expect a void-returning method.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the Pneumatic.raisePressure method signature consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement UML and any textual references so raisePressure(int) returns void (replace ': boolean' with ': void'), or (B) change the solution and template Pneumatic interface to declare 'boolean raisePressure(int pressureIncrease);' and update all implementing classes to return a boolean (e.g., stub 'return false;'). Option A is simpler if the intended behavior is no return value; Option B should be used only if the method is intended to indicate success/failure via the return value.
